title: Introduce credential-orchestra and iterable stability bridge (py/ts/go parity + version bumps)
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: This PR delivers a coordinated TypeScript-first implementation of a lightweight 'credential-orchestra' (cred mediator) and a small compatibility bridge for iterable streaming consumers. Motivation: multiple customers and internal SDK parity audits showed drift between Python/Go/TS around credential fallback semantics and stream-iterator signals (pause/resume/heartbeat). Instead of a heavy refactor across all SDKs at once, this change introduces a compact mediator pattern + an adapter surface that preserves existing ergonomics while enabling consistent retry/backoff behavior and clearer telemetry.
commits: Summary of commits: 1) init: credential-orchestra core (types + in-memory registry + tests) 2) adapter: pullstream -> async-iterable bridge with graceful backoff hooks 3) auth: unify token refresh predicate and expose refresh hints to consumer 4) tests: cross-sdk compatibility fixtures and smoke e2e 5) docs + changelog + version bump to 1.8.0
changed_files: src/auth/credentialOrchestra.ts - core mediator and registry implementation
src/stream/iterableBridge.ts - adapter between push/pull and async-iterators
tests/e2e/stream-smoke.test.ts - e2e smoke harness against local runtime
CHANGELOG.md - entry for credential-orchestra and iterator stability
scripts/ci/compat-runner.sh - small harness to run tri-sdk fixtures
review_comments: Dmitry Ivanov: Please ensure token refresh predicate is non-blocking for long-lived streams — we saw 50ms tail in local test. (reply from author) Ava: switched to a non-blocking compare+signal pattern, added unit test to cover long-lived stream with refresh at 10s intervals.

Lena Cho: Adapter looks good. Suggest moving the default backoff profile to a shared util so Go/Python can later import similar semantics. (author) Ava: extracted backoffProfiles.ts and added a small JSON schema so the Go impl can reuse the same profile definitions.

Marcus Reed: CI failed once on macOS node for flaky e2e; did you pin the timeout? (author) Ava: yes — increased e2e timeout and added retry wrapper for the local harness; also added a smoke job to avoid regressions.
QA (internal): Confirmed no behavior change for existing clients when using default credential chain; new behavior only enabled when 'credentialOrchestra.enable' is set to true in client config.
merge_outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Dmitry and Lena. Release note added; publish job triggered to stage registry. Small follow-up fixes (tests and docs) were merged in a separate PR that adjusted wording in the upgrade guide.
release_notes:
- Introduce credential-orchestra (opt-in) to centralize credential fallback and refresh signals across long-lived streams.
- Add iterable bridge adapter to smooth parity gaps between push/pull stream shapes in TS/Python/Go.
- Expose standardized backoff profile schema for inter-SDK reuse.
- Bump TypeScript SDK to 1.8.0 (non-breaking, opt-in features).
notes_for_backport: No backport required. The change is opt-in behind a config flag; backport only if enterprise customers request a patch to the previous minor release.
manual_steps_after_merge: 1) Announce opt-in flag and migration doc in SDK-release channel. 2) Coordinate small follow-up PRs in Python/Go repos to consume the backoff schema (ENG-8302). 3) Watch compat-runner for next 48 hours for flakiness.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover mediator registration, lookup and refresh signal; adapter tests validate pause/resume semantics under token rotation; compat-runner executed against Python/Go fixtures to ensure signal shapes are equivalent. Local perf microbench showed <2% additional CPU on typical streaming workloads when mediator is enabled.
followups: Create Python shim that imports backoff profile JSON and mirrors refresh-hint headers (PR planned: python/cred-orchestra-adopt-1034)
Add Go minimal adapter to reuse backoff profile (PR planned: go/stream-bridge-421)
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default behavior unchanged; risk concentrated on opt-in flows and long-lived streams where token refresh timing matters. Mitigations: extra e2e smoke tests, telemetry on refresh errors, ability to disable via flag.
